axes.model_access: Models are orchestrated and routed on the Manus side (no complete model list published officially); users do not pick models directly — "which model does the work" is an internal product decision, one of its key differences from general chat products.
axes.runtime: Tasks run in Manus's cloud sandbox (the sandbox surface on the manus.computer domain, as seen via direct fetch): the agent executes code, browses the web and produces files inside a cloud VM; the web UI issues and follows up, nothing is installed locally.
axes.local_files: Artifacts (files/web pages/reports) are generated in the cloud sandbox and can be downloaded/exported; uploaded data is stored on the account side. The exact opposite of a "local agent" — the execution surface is on the vendor's cloud.
axes.background: Asynchronous tasks are its native form: after submitting a task you can leave the page and the agent keeps running in the cloud (the official narrative is "hand the task to it"); there are productization traces of grace-period/queueing mechanics (credit system and concurrency limits).
axes.tools: Built-in tool surfaces incl. browser, code execution, file operations and deployment (the manus.space publishing surface); connecting external services (email/calendar etc.) goes through official integration lines. MCP support not verified item by item.
axes.context: Work is organized per task (session); no official statement verified for a cross-task memory mechanism.
axes.permissions: Account + subscription system; the cloud sandbox has network egress (browsing/downloading is product semantics); data retention and training terms are governed by the official Terms/Privacy, details not verified item by item.
axes.fit: Suits: handing whole tasks (research reports, data tidying, site building & publishing) asynchronously to a cloud agent, with artifacts published directly (manus.space). Does not suit: picking models, local files participating in execution, or heavy free use (credit system).

runs:
This site has not completed measured runs. The coding-oriented test protocol is at [protocols/coding/_protocol.md](../../../protocols/coding/_protocol.md) (the coding task suite does not apply to chat products).

**Suggested measurements** (three, all pointing at things the official readable pages do not give):

- **Credit-deduction rules when a task fails/is interrupted** (a credit-based product; billing on failure is what users care about most)
- **The network egress scope of the cloud sandbox** (which domains it can reach, whether intranet-type services are reachable)
- **Retention and access control of artifacts on manus.space**
unknowns:
- The model-orchestration list (not published officially)
- Details of data retention and training terms (Terms/Privacy direct-fetched but clauses not verified line by line)
- The cross-task memory mechanism (no official statement verified)
- Filing status (no public-registry entry verified)
related: Also a cloud async agent: Devin's main axis is codebases, Manus's main axis is general tasks.
